n0.hypothesis: Improve root errors without sacrificing duration-weighted majmin accuracy
n0.insight:
[from n4] Retain complete chord accuracy as primary; low-register weighting alone did not improve this recognizer.
[from n3] Discrete note profiles before octave folding are promising; modeled harmonic subtraction is not supported as the source of the best gain.
[from n5] Use note-level projection as an exploratory low-cost candidate. No replacement of the baseline is supported by the saturated isolated-chord test; further transfer claims need unevaluated chord progressions.

n2.hypothesis: Low-register evidence improves root choice despite inversion ambiguity
n2.insight: [from n4] Retain complete chord accuracy as primary; low-register weighting alone did not improve this recognizer.

metadata.prune_reason: Four low-register mixtures failed to improve development major/minor accuracy.

n3.hypothesis: Before octave folding, fit note spectra by NNLS with harmonic decay 0.6 or 0.9; compare a fundamental-only dictionary control
n3.insight: The improvement does not require explicit harmonic partials. A direct-projection control is needed to separate note-profile resolution from iterative fitting.

metadata.result: Fundamental-only NNLS78.36555%, root80.14528%; harmonic0.6=73.07294%, harmonic0.9=63.19797%, baseline71.96540%. Both development families improve for decay0.

n4.hypothesis: Mix low-register root or triad evidence at weights 0.1 and 0.2 with the frozen full-register triad scores
n4.insight: A lower root-error rate can accompany worse complete chord identification; root-specific evidence must retain quality accuracy.

metadata.result: All four low-register mixtures lower major/minor accuracy. Best changed setting71.9204vs71.9654%; rootaccuracy+0.31points is offset by more qualityerrors.

n5.hypothesis: Direct projection onto fundamental-only note profiles matches the NNLS gain at lower cost
n5.insight: Tuned fundamental note profiles recover most of the development gain without a joint NNLS solve. The isolated-chord comparison has a ceiling and cannot establish progression-level transfer.

metadata.result: Direct projection reached 78.024857% majmin and 79.542095% root accuracy on development data, below NNLS by 0.340693 percentage points in majmin; both progression families improved over baseline. Fresh isolated-chord decoded accuracy tied baseline and NNLS at 100%.
